rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 (base_speed 1.7, kp 3.0, ki 1.0, kd 0.5, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction) is the best raced design at 299.69. Oval finishes rose from 4/20 to 14/20, mean oval finish time was 1.90 s, and oval progress reached 0.91. The iteration 9 reproduction confirmed that the iteration 7 base (216.97) is stable under the same seeds, so the gain is attributable to the speed change.

The Evaluator's conditional rule for trying base_speed 1.8 is not met. s-bend progress fell from 0.462 to 0.264 with all 20 runs off track, slalom progress fell from 0.124 to 0.102, and the s-bend steering_oscillation was 0.214. So the bends are weaker at 1.7 even though the oval is better. The rule's fallback (return base_speed to 1.6) applies only if the score falls below 216.97, which it did not.

Decision: submit the iteration 10 design unchanged. It is the best confirmed result, and this is the final iteration with no later race to check any new change. A further step to 1.8 would be an untested change that also risks the bends, which already regressed at 1.7. The Evaluator's R1 entity is identical to this design and its 'written before raced' feedback is stale, so I treat its approval as applying to a known candidate.

Expected result: about 300 on the development tracks, with oval finish rate near 0.7. Watch item for the unseen final track: bend progress, since s-bend progress dropped at 1.7. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation.
